intro: The most common English verbs (go, have, make, see, take…) are irregular: their past simple does not end in -ed, so you must learn it. Good news: negatives and questions work exactly as with regular verbs.
objectifs: Know the past simple of about forty very common irregular verbs.
Learn irregular verbs in groups with similar forms, not as a long list.
Use didn't and Did …? with the base verb, even for irregular verbs.
Tell the story of a trip or a day with regular and irregular verbs.

texte: An irregular verb has a special past form: go → went, see → saw, buy → bought. As with regular verbs, the form is the same for every subject (I went, she went, they went).

Lists of irregular verbs have three columns: base form, past simple, past participle (go – went – gone). In this lesson, only the second column matters. The past participle is for the present perfect (lesson 51).
exemples: I went to Kribi last weekend.
She bought a new phone yesterday.
have → had; “have a great time” = enjoy yourself

texte: There are about 150 common irregular verbs, but about fifty are enough for daily life. They are easier to remember in families with similar forms.

the most frequent verbs in English: learn these first

sections.note: Tip: learn five verbs a day and say one true sentence with each (“Yesterday I drank three coffees”). Personal sentences help you remember the form.

sections.titre: Negatives and questions: back to the base
texte: In negatives and questions, the irregular form disappears: did / didn't shows the past, and the main verb goes back to its base form. It is the same rule as for regular verbs (lesson 41).
Be careful with “to be”: it never uses did. We say “I wasn't”, “Were you…?” (lesson 39).
exemples: We didn't take the bus; we took a taxi.
What did you buy at the market?
Did you hear the news? — Yes, I did.

texte: “Do” is both a helper verb and a main verb. In the past, the main verb “do” becomes “did”. So you can see did and do in the same sentence.
This is not a mistake: the first one is the helper, the second one is the main verb.
exemples: What did you do on Sunday?

texte: Some past forms look like other words, so be careful.
read → read: same spelling, but different sounds (/riːd/ now, /red/ in the past). The context and the time word tell you the tense.
leave → left (go away) but live → lived (have your home); feel → felt (have a feeling) but fall → fell (go down to the ground); lose → lost (not find) but loose is an adjective (not tight).
exemples: I read that book last year.
He fell and felt a pain in his knee.

formule: subject + irregular past (went, saw, took…) · didn't + base · Did + subject + base …?
prononciation: All -ought / -aught forms sound /ɔːt/: bought /bɔːt/, thought /θɔːt/, taught /tɔːt/, caught /kɔːt/. The gh is silent.
“saw” /sɔː/ sounds like “sore” in British English; “ate” is /et/ (UK) or /eɪt/ (UK and US).
“went” /went/ has a short e as in “pet”; do not confuse it with “wanted” /ˈwɒntɪd/ (from want).
erreurs: After did, always use the base verb.
didn't + base, even with an irregular verb.
With yesterday, use the past simple (took).

dialogue.contexte: Fatou is back from a trip to Canada. Her friend Claire calls her from Lyon.
lignes: How was…? = a question with “to be”.
Amazing! I flew to Montreal and then I took the train to Quebec City.
Yes, I did! It was minus fifteen. I bought a big coat on the first day.
I ate poutine three times. And I met some very friendly people.
Did you speak French or English?
Both! But I didn't understand the Quebec accent at first.

mots: We had a short trip to Ghent.
a journey to a place and back again
I flew to Montreal in May.
to get something by paying money
to see and talk to someone, by plan or by chance
to go away from a place
I spent a week in Dakar.
to not be able to find something
to know the meaning of something
to take something or someone with you to a place

exercices.consigne: Write the past simple of each irregular verb.
Put the verbs in the past simple.
items: Last year I ___ (go) to Belgium for the first time.
I ___ (leave) Douala on a Friday night.
The flight ___ (be) long, so I ___ (sleep) a lot.
In Brussels I ___ (meet) my cousin at the station.
We ___ (have) dinner and ___ (drink) some hot chocolate.

exercices.consigne: Change the sentence as shown in brackets.
Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
Write a question about the part in CAPITALS.
items: I forgot MY PHONE at home.
What did you forget at home?
They came to the party AT NINE.
When did they come to the party?

exercices.consigne: Write five or six sentences about a trip or a day out, with at least five different irregular verbs.
items: Last month I went to Ghent with two friends. We took the train from Brussels and got there at ten. We saw the old castle and ate waffles in a small café. I bought a postcard for my mother. We didn't spend much money, but we had a wonderful day.

a_retenir: The most common verbs are irregular: went, had, did, made, saw, took, got, said…
One past form for all subjects.
Negatives and questions: didn't / Did + base (didn't go, Did you see…?).
“to be” never uses did: wasn't, weren't, Was…? Were…?
Learn verbs in groups (bought / thought / taught; slept / felt / kept…).
